Burkhart created the storytelling artwork to explore the area’s history through visual elements. ROSCOMMON COUNTY, Mich., (WPBN/WGTU) -- Roscommon County has its first confirmed case of chronic wasting disease in a farmed cervid, the Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development says. The animal was identified through the state’s surveillance program. Cervids are members of the deer family, including white-tailed deer, mule deer, elk and moose. Chronic wasting disease is a fatal neurological illness that can affect deer, elk, moose and other cervids. It can spread between animals and through the environment.
